shucker: One who shucks oysters or clams
shirting: Cloth, specifically cotton cloth, suitable for making shirts.

shunless: Not to be shunned; inevitable; unavoidable. "Shunless destiny." Shak.

shinney: The game of hockey; -- so called because of the liability of the players to receive blows on the shin. Halliwell.
sharpwitted: Having an acute or nicely discerning mind.
shapable: 1. That may be shaped. 2. Shapely. "Round and shapable." De Foe.

shrapnel: Applied as an appellation to a kind of shell invented by Gen. H. Shrapnel of the British army. -- n. A shrapnel shell; shrapnel shells, collectively. shyness: The quality or state of being shy. [Written also shiness.] Frequency in heavenly contemplation is particularly important to prevent a shyness bewtween God and thy soul. Baxter. Syn. -- Bashfulness; reserve; coyness; timidity; diffidence. See Bashfulness.
sheath: 1. A case for the reception of a sword, hunting knife, or other long and slender instrument; a scabbard. The dead knight's sword out of his sheath he drew. Spenser. 2. shoddyism: The quality or state of being shoddy. [Colloq.] See the Note under Shoddy, n.
shakefork: A fork for shaking hay; a pitchfork. (old)
shimmering: A gleam or glimmering. "A little shimmering of a light." Chaucer.
shortwinded: Affected with shortness of breath; having a quick, difficult respiration, as dyspnoic and asthmatic persons. May.
shaitan: 1. Among Mohammedans: (a) An evil spirit; the evil one; the devil. (b) One of bad disposition; a fiend. [Colloq.] 2. (Meteor.) A dust storm. [India]
shiprigged: Rigged like a ship, that is, having three masts, each with square sails.
shagrag: The unkempt and ragged part of the community. [Colloq. or Slang.] R. Browning.
shipmaster: The captain, master, or commander of a ship. Jonah i. 6.
shote: 1. (Zoöl.) A fish resembling the trout. [Obs. or Prov. Eng.] Garew. 2. Etym: [Perh. a different word.] A young hog; a shoat.

shoggle: To joggle. [Obs. or Prov. Eng. & Scot.] Pegge.
shook: imp. & obs. or poet. p. p. of Shake. | (a) A set of staves and headings sufficient in number for one hogshead, cask, barrel, or the like, trimmed, and bound together in compact form. (b) A set of boards for a sugar box.
shedder: 1. One who, or that which, sheds; as, a shedder of blood; a shedder of tears. 2. (Zoöl.) A crab in the act of casting its shell, or immediately afterwards while still soft; -- applied especially to the edible crabs, which are most prized while in this state.
sheth: The part of a plow which projects downward beneath the beam, for holding the share and other working parts; -- also called standard, or post.
sheeny: Bright; shining; radiant; sheen. "A sheeny summer morn." Tennyson.
shakespearean: Of, pertaining to, or in the style of, Shakespeare or his works. [Written also Shakespearian, Shakspearean, Shakspearian, Shaksperean, Shaksperian.etc.]
shirred: 1. (Sewing) Made or gathered into a shirr; as, a shirred bonnet. 2. (Cookery) Broken into an earthen dish and baked over the fire; -- said of eggs.

shears: 1. A cutting instrument. Specifically: (a) An instrument consisting of two blades, commonly with bevel edges, connected by a pivot, and working on both sides of the material to be cut, -- used for cutting cloth and other substances. Fate urged the shears, and cut the sylph in twain. Pope.

shizoku: The Japanese warrior gentry or middle class, formerly called samurai; also, any member of this class.

sheepmaster: A keeper or feeder of sheep; also, an owner of sheep. 2 Kings iii. 4.

shruff: Rubbish. Specifically: (a) Dross or refuse of metals. (old) (b) Light, dry wood, or stuff used for fuel. [Prov. Eng.]
sherryvallies: Trousers or overalls of thick cloth or leather, buttoned on the outside of each leg, and generally worn to protect other trousers when riding on horseback. [Local, U.S.] Bartlett.
shawnees: A tribe of North American Indians who occupied Western New York and part of Ohio, but were driven away and widely dispersed by the Iroquois.
shots: The refuse of cattle taken from a drove. [Prov. Eng.] Halliwell.
shagginess: The quality or state of being shaggy; roughness; shaggedness.
shall: 1. To owe; to be under obligation for. (old) "By the faith I shall to God" Court of Love. 2. To be obliged; must. (old) "Me athinketh [I am sorry] that I shall rehearse it her." Chaucer. 3. sharebroker: A broker who deals in railway or other shares and securities.

shamer: One who, or that which, disgraces, or makes ashamed. Beau & Fl.
shammer: One who shams; an impostor. Johnson.
shoefly: 1. (Railroading) A contrivance for throwing the track temporarily to one side for convenience in filling washouts or effecting other repairs. [Cant, U. S.] 2. (Print.) In some cylinder presses, a device with long fingers for freeing the sheet from the cylinder.
shellless: , a. Having no shell. J. Burroughs.

shyly: In a shy or timid manner; not familiarly; with reserve. [Written also shily.]

shouldered: Having shoulders; -- used in composition; as, a broad- shouldered man. "He was short-shouldered." Chaucer.

shopworn: Somewhat worn or damaged by having been kept for a time in a shop.
shipload: The load, or cargo, of a ship.

shopkeeper: A trader who sells goods in a shop, or by retail; -- in distinction from one who sells by wholesale. Addison.

shrilltongued: Having a shrill voice. "When shrill-tongued Fulvia scolds." Shak.

sheathy: Forming or resembling a sheath or case. Sir T. Browne.

shadowiness: The quality or state of being shadowy.
shelly: Abounding with shells; consisting of shells, or of a shell. "The shelly shore." Prior. Shrinks backward in his shelly cave. Shak.
shellbark: A species of hickory (Carya alba) whose outer bark is loose and peeling; a shagbark; also, its nut.

shallot: A small kind of onion (Allium Ascalonicum) growing in clusters, and ready for gathering in spring; a scallion, or eschalot.
shearman: One whose occupation is to shear cloth.

shad: Any one of several species of food fishes of the Herring family. shintiism: One of the two great systems of religious belief in Japan. Its essence is ancestor worship, and sacrifice to dead heroes. [Written also Sintu, and Sintuism.]
shuntvalve: A valve permitting a fluid under pressure an easier avenue of escape than normally; specif., a valve, actuated by the governor, used in one system of marine-engine governing to connect both ends of the low-pressure cylinder as a supplementary control.
shepherdess: A woman who tends sheep; hence, a rural lass. She put herself into the garb of a shepherdess. Sir P. Sidney.
shrap: A place baited with chaff to entice birds. [Written also scrap.] (old) Bp. Bedell.

shredding: 1. The act of cutting or tearing into shreds. 2. That which is cut or torn off; a piece. Hooker.

shintyan: A kind of wide loose drawers or trousers worn by women in Mohammedan countries.

showing: 1. Appearance; display; exhibition. 2. Presentation of facts; statement. J. S. Mill.
shoaly: Full of shoals, or shallow places. The tossing vessel sailed on shoaly ground. Dryden.

sharking: Petty rapine; trick; also, seeking a livelihood by shifts and dishonest devices.

shastra: A treatise for authoritative instruction among the Hindoos; a book of institutes; especially, a treatise explaining the Vedas. [Written also sastra.]

shuffling: 1. Moving with a dragging, scraping step. "A shuffling nag." Shak. 2. Evasive; as, a shuffling excuse. T. Burnet.

shafted: 1. Furnished with a shaft, or with shafts; as, a shafted arch. 2. (Her.) Having a shaft; -- applied to a spear when the head and the shaft are of different tinctures.
shaddock: A tree (Citrus decumana) and its fruit, which is a large species of orange; -- called also forbidden fruit, and pompelmous.
shock: 1. A pile or assemblage of sheaves of grain, as wheat, rye, or the like, set up in a field, the sheaves varying in number from twelve to sixteen; a stook. And cause it on shocks to be by and by set. | To collect, or make up, into a shock or shocks; to stook; as, to shock rye.
shuck: 1. A shell, husk, or pod; especially, the outer covering of such nuts as the hickory nut, butternut, peanut, and chestnut. 2. The shell of an oyster or clam. [U. S.] | To deprive of the shucks or husks; as, to shuck walnuts, Indian corn, oysters, etc.
shrillness: The quality or state of being shrill.
sheldaple: A chaffinch. [Written also sheldapple, and shellapple.]
shrape: A place baited with chaff to entice birds. [Written also scrap.] (old) Bp. Bedell.
shorthorn: One of a breed of large, heavy domestic cattle having short horns. The breed was developed in England.
sharpcut: Cut sharply or definitely, or so as to make a clear, well- defined impression, as the lines of an engraved plate, and the like; clear-cut; hence, having great distinctness; well-defined; clear.
shako: A kind of military cap or headress.
shebang: A jocosely depreciative name for a dwelling or shop. [Slang,U.S.]
shading: 1. Act or process of making a shade. 2. That filling up which represents the effect of more or less darkness, expressing rotundity, projection, etc., in a picture or a drawing.
shiver: 1. One of the small pieces, or splinters, into which a brittle thing is broken by sudden violence; -- generally used in the plural. "All to shivers dashed." Milton. 2. A thin slice; a shive. [Obs. | To break into many small pieces, or splinters; to shatter; to dash to pieces by a blow; as, to shiver a glass goblet. All the ground With shivered armor strown. Milton.
shaveling: A man shaved; hence, a monk, or other religious; -- used in contempt. I am no longer a shaveling than while my frock is on my back. Sir W. Scott.
shagged: Shaggy; rough. Milton. -- Shag"ged*ness, n. Dr. H. More.
sherd: A fragment; -- now used only in composition, as in potsherd. See Shard. The thigh . . . which all in sherds it drove. Chapman.
shotted: 1. Loaded with shot. 2. (Med.) Having a shot attached; as, a shotten suture.
shingles: A kind of herpes (Herpes zoster) which spreads half way around the body like a girdle, and is usually attended with violent neuralgic pain.
shaft: 1. The slender, smooth stem of an arrow; hence, an arrow. His sleep, his meat, his drink, is him bereft, That lean he wax, and dry as is a shaft. Chaucer. A shaft hath three principal parts, the stele [stale], the feathers, and the head. Ascham. 2. The long handle of a spear or similar weapon; hence, the weapon itself;
sharpshooter: One skilled in shooting at an object with exactness; a good marksman.
shopboy: A boy employed in a shop.
shamble: 1. (Mining) One of a succession of niches or platforms, one above another, to hold ore which is thrown successively from platform to platform, and thus raised to a higher level. 2. pl. | To walk awkwardly and unsteadily, as if the knees were weak; to shuffle along.
shapeliness: The quality or state of being shapely.
sheepshearer: One who shears, or cuts off the wool from, sheep.
shire: 1. A portion of Great Britain originally under the supervision of an earl; a territorial division, usually identical with a county, but sometimes limited to a smaller district; as, Wiltshire, Yorkshire, Richmondshire, Hallamshire. An indefinite number of these hundreds make up a county or shire. Blackstone. 2. A division of a State, embracing several contiguous townships;
shambling: Characterized by an awkward, irregular pace; as, a shambling trot; shambling legs.
shafiite: A member of one of the four sects of the Sunnites, or Orthodox Mohammedans; -- so called from its founder, Mohammed al-Shafeï.
shrimp: 1. (Zoöl.) (a) Any one of numerous species of macruran Crustacea belonging to Crangon and various allied genera, having a slender body and long legs. Many of them are used as food. The larger kinds are called also prawns. See Illust. of Decapoda.
shrouded: Provided with a shroud or shrouds. Shrouded gear (Mach.), a cogwheel or pinion having flanges which form closed ends to the spaces between the teeth and thus strengthen the teeth by tying them together.
sharpsighted: Having quick or acute sight; -- used literally and figuratively. -- Sharp`-sight`ed*ness, n.
shipboard: A ship's side; hence, by extension, a ship; -- found chiefly in adverbial phrases; as, on shipboard; a shipboard.
shamefast: Modest; shamefaced. -- Shame"fast*ly, adv. -- Shame"fast*ness, n. (old) See Shamefaced. Shamefast she was in maiden shamefastness. Chaucer. [Conscience] is a blushing shamefast spirit. Shak. Modest apparel with shamefastness. 1 Tim. ii. 9 (Rev. Ver.).
shroffage: The examination of coins, and the separation of the good from the debased. [East Indies]
shinto: One of the two great systems of religious belief in Japan. Its essence is ancestor worship, and sacrifice to dead heroes. [Written also Sintu, and Sintuism.]
shoe: 1. A covering for the human foot, usually made of leather, having a thick and somewhat stiff sole and a lighter top. It differs from a boot on not extending so far up the leg. | 1. To furnish with a shoe or shoes; to put a shoe or shoes on; as, to shoe a horse, a sled, an anchor. 2. To protect or ornament with something which serves the purpose of a shoe; to tip.
shapely: 1. Well-formed; having a regular shape; comely; symmetrical. T. Warton. Waste sandy valleys, once perplexed with thorn, The spiry fir and shapely box adorn. Pope. Where the shapely column stood. Couper. 2. Fit; suitable. (old) Shaply for to be an alderman. Chaucer.
shag: 1. Coarse hair or nap; rough, woolly hair. True Witney broadcloth, with its shag unshorn. Gay. 2. A kind of cloth having a long, coarse nap. 3. (Com.) A kind of prepared tobacco cut fine. 4. | To make hairy or shaggy; hence, to make rough. Shag the green zone that bounds the boreal skies. J. Barlow.
shovelhead: A shark (Sphryna tiburio) allied to the hammerhead, and native of the warmer parts of the Atlantic and Pacific oceans; -- called also bonnet shark.
shipful: As much or as many as a ship will hold; enough to fill a ship.
shebeen: A low public house; especially, a place where spirits and other excisable liquors are illegally and privately sold. [Ireland]
shebander: A harbor master, or ruler of a port, in the East Indies. [Written also shebunder.]
shab: The itch in animals; also, a scab. [Obs. or Prov. Eng.] | To play mean tricks; to act shabbily. [Obs. or Prov.Eng.]
shrove: imp. of Shrive. Shrove Sunday, Quinguagesima Sunday. -- Shrove Tuesday, the Tuesday following Quinguagesima Sunday, and preceding the first day of Lent, or Ash Wednesday. | To join in the festivities of Shrovetide; hence, to make merry. (old) J. Fletcher.
shrovetide: The days immediately preceding Ash Widnesday, especially the period between the evening before Quinguagesima Sunday and the morning of Ash Wednesday.
shorten: 1. To make short or shorter in measure, extent, or time; as, to shorten distance; to shorten a road; to shorten days of calamity. 2. To reduce or diminish in amount, quantity, or extent; to lessen; | To become short or shorter; as, the day shortens in northern latitudes from June to December; a metallic rod shortens by cold.
sheathed: 1. Povided with, or inclosed in, sheath. 2. (Bot.) Invested by a sheath, or cylindrical membranaceous tube, which is the base of the leaf, as the stalk or culm in grasses; vaginate.
shug: 1. To writhe the body so as to produce friction against one's clothes, as do those who have the itch. [Prov. Eng.] Halliwell. 2. Hence, to crawl; to sneak. (old) There I 'll shug in and get a noble countenance. Ford.
shovelnosed: Having a broad, flat nose; as, the shovel-nosed duck, or shoveler.
shooi: The Richardson's skua (Stercorarius parasiticus);- so called from its cry. [Prov. Eng.]
shirr: A series of close parallel runnings which are drawn up so as to make the material between them set full by gatherings; -- called also shirring, and gauging.
shakudo: An alloy of copper, invented by the Japanese, having a very dark blue color approaching black.
shallon: An evergreen shrub (Gaultheria Shallon) of Northwest America; also, its fruit. See Salal-berry.
shogunate: The office or dignity of a Shogun. [Written also Siogoonate.]
showman: One who exhibits a show; a proprietor of a show.
shipyard: A yard, place, or inclosure where ships are built or repaired.
shotten: 1. Having ejected the spawn; as, a shotten herring. Shak. 2. Shot out of its socket; dislocated, as a bone.
shoder: A package of gold beater's skins in which gold is subjected to the second process of beating.
shop: imp. of Shape. Shaped. Chaucer. | 1. A building or an apartment in which goods, wares, drugs, etc., are sold by retail. From shop to shop Wandering, and littering with unfolded silks The polished counter. Cowper. 2.
shet: To shut. [Obs. or Prov. Eng.] Chaucer.
shaver: 1. One who shaves; one whose occupation is to shave. 2. One who is close in bargains; a sharper. Swift. 3. One who fleeces; a pillager; a plunderer. By these shavers the Turks were stripped. Knolles. 4. A boy; a lad; a little fellow. [Colloq.] "These unlucky little shavers." Salmagundi.
shoebill: A large African wading bird (Balæniceps rex) allied to the storks and herons, and remarkable for its enormous broad swollen bill. It inhabits the valley of the White Nile. See Illust. (l.) of Beak.
sheepsplit: A split of a sheepskin; one of the thin sections made by splitting a sheepskin with a cutting knife or machine.
shrewd: 1. Inclining to shrew; disposing to curse or scold; hence, vicious; malicious; evil; wicked; mischievous; vexatious; rough; unfair; shrewish. (old) Chaucer. [Egypt] hath many shrewd havens, because of the great rocks that ben strong and dangerous to pass by. Sir J. Mandeville. Every of this happy number That have endured shrewd days and nights with us. Shak. 2. Artful; wily;
shaving: 1. The act of one who, or that which, shaves; specifically, the act of cutting off the beard with a razor. 2. That which is shaved off; a thin slice or strip pared off with a shave, a knife, a plane, or other cutting instrument. "Shaving of silver." Chaucer. Shaving brush, a brush used in lathering the face preparatory to shaving it.
sheldafle: A chaffinch. [Written also sheldapple, and shellapple.]
shotsamples: Samples taken for assay from a molten metallic mass pouring a portion into water, to granulate it.
shape: 1. To form or create; especially, to mold or make into a particular form; to give proper form or figure to. I was shapen in iniquity. Ps. li. 5. Grace shaped her limbs, and beauty decked her face. | To suit; to be adjusted or conformable. Shak.
sharpset: Eager in appetite or desire of gratification; affected by keen hunger; ravenous; as, an eagle or a lion sharp-set. The town is sharp-set on new plays. Pope.
sheepshearing: 1. Act of shearing sheep. 2. A feast at the time of sheep-shearing. Shak.
shameful: 1. Bringing shame or disgrace; injurious to reputation; disgraceful. His naval preparations were not more surprising than his quick and shameful retreat. Arbuthnot. 2. Exciting the feeling of shame in others; indecent; as, a shameful picture; a shameful sight. Spenser. Syn. -- Disgraceful; reproachful; indecent; unbecoming; degrading; scandalous; ignominious; infamous.
shaster: A treatise for authoritative instruction among the Hindoos; a book of institutes; especially, a treatise explaining the Vedas. [Written also sastra.]
sheelfa: The chaffinch; -- so named from its call note. [Prov. Eng.]
shandygaff: A mixture of strong beer and ginger beer. [Eng.]
sheepberry: The edible fruit of a small North American tree of the genus Viburnum (V. Lentago), having white flowers in flat cymes; also, the tree itself. Called also nannyberry.
shortbreathed: 1. Having short-breath, or quick respiration. 2. Having short life.
shippo: Cloisonné enamel on a background of metal or porcelain.
shittahtree: A tree that furnished the precious wood of which the ark, tables, altars, boards, etc., of the Jewish tabernacle were made; -- now believed to have been the wood of the Acacia Seyal, which is hard, fine grained, and yellowish brown in color.
shealing: The outer husk, pod, or shell, as of oats, pease, etc.; sheal; shell. [Obs. or Prov. Eng. & Scot.]
shade: 1. Comparative obscurity owing to interception or interruption of the rays of light; partial darkness caused by the intervention of something between the space contemplated and the source of light. | 1. To shelter or screen by intercepting the rays of light; to keep off illumination from. Milton. I went to crop the sylvan scenes, And shade our altars with their leafy greens. Dryden. 2.
sharer: One who shares; a participator; a partaker; also, a divider; a distributer.
shrillgorged: Having a throat which produces a shrill note. Shak.
sheading: A tithing, or division, in the Isle of Man, in which there is a coroner, or chief constable. The island is divided into six sheadings.
shaker: 1. A person or thing that shakes, or by means of which something is shaken. 2. One of a religious sect who do not marry, popularly so called from the movements of the members in dancing, which forms a part of their worship. Note: The sect originated in England in 1747, and came to the United States in 1774, under the leadership of Mother Ann Lee.
sheathe: 1. To put into a sheath, case, or scabbard; to inclose or cover with, or as with, a sheath or case. The leopard . . . keeps the claws of his fore feet turned up from the ground, and sheathed in the skin of his toes. Grew. 'T is in my breast she sheathes her dagger now. Dryden. 2. To fit or furnish, as with a sheath. Shak. 3.
shipman: A seaman, or sailor. [Obs. or Poetic] Chaucer. R. Browning. About midnight the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country. Acts xxvii. 27. Shipman's card, the mariner's compass. (old) Shak.
sheafy: Pertaining to, or consisting of, a sheaf or sheaves; resembling a sheaf.
shovelful: As much as a shovel will hold; enough to fill a shovel.
shrike: Any one of numerous species of oscinine birds of the family Laniidæ, having a strong hooked bill, toothed at the tip. Most shrikes are insectivorous, but the common European gray shrike (Lanius excubitor), the great northern shrike (L.
shadowing: 1. Shade, or gradation of light and color; shading. Feltham. 2. A faint representation; an adumbration. There are . . . in savage theology shadowings, quaint or majestic, of the conception of a Supreme Deity. Tylor.
shelvy: Sloping gradually; shelving. The shore was shelving and shallow. Shak.
shawm: A wind instrument of music, formerly in use, supposed to have resembled either the clarinet or the hautboy in form. [Written also shalm, shaum.] Otway. Even from the shrillest shaum unto the cornamute. Drayton.
shillelah: An oaken sapling or cudgel; any cudgel; -- so called from Shillelagh, a place in Ireland of that name famous for its oaks. [Irish] [Written also shillaly, and shillely.]
shorage: Duty paid for goods brought on shore. Grabb.
shippen: A stable; a cowhouse. [Obs. or Prov.Eng.]
sham: 1. That which deceives expectation; any trick, fraud, or device that deludes and disappoint; a make-believe; delusion; imposture, humbug. "A mere sham." Bp. Stillingfleet. | False; counterfeit; pretended; feigned; unreal; as, a sham fight. They scorned the sham independence proffered to them by the Athenians. Jowett (Thucyd)
shirtless: Not having or wearing a shirt. Pope. -- Shirt"less*ness, n.
sheriff: The chief officer of a shire or county, to whom is intrusted the execution of the laws, the serving of judicial writs and processes, and the preservation of the peace. Note: In England, sheriffs are appointed by the king. In the United States, sheriffs are elected by the legislature or by the citizens, or appointed and commissioned by the executive of the State.
shepherdia: A genus of shrubs having silvery scurfy leaves, and belonging to the same family as Elæagnus; also, any plant of this genus. See Buffalo berry, under Buffalo.
shedding: 1. The act of shedding, separating, or casting off or out; as, the shedding of blood. 2. That which is shed, or cast off. Wordsworth.
shendship: Harm; ruin; also, reproach; disgrace. (old) Chaucer.
should: Used as an auxiliary verb, to express a conditional or contingent act or state, or as a supposition of an actual fact; also, to express moral obligation (see Shall); e. g.: they should have come last week; if I should go; I should think you could go. "You have done that you should be sorry for." Shak. Syn. -- See Ought.
shoal: A great multitude assembled; a crowd; a throng; -- said especially of fish; as, a shoal of bass. "Great shoals of people." Bacon. Beneath, a shoal of silver fishes glides. Waller. | To assemble in a multitude; to throng; as, the fishes shoaled about the place. Chapman.
shardborne: Borne on shards or scaly wing cases. "The shard-borne beetle." Shak.
shudder: To tremble or shake with fear, horrer, or aversion; to shiver with cold; to quake. "With shuddering horror pale." Milton. The shuddering tennant of the frigid zone. Goldsmith. | The act of shuddering, as with fear. Shak.
shandrydan: A jocosely depreciative name for a vehicle. [Ireland]
shortcake: An unsweetened breakfast cake shortened with butter or lard, rolled thin, and baked.
shahin: A large and swift Asiatic falcon (Falco pregrinator) highly valued in falconry.
shipment: 1. The act or process of shipping; as, he was engaged in the shipment of coal for London; an active shipment of wheat from the West. 2. That which is shipped. The question is, whether the share of M. in the shipment is exempted from condemnation by reason of his neutral domicle. Story.
shift: 1. To divide; to distribute; to apportion. (old) To which God of his bounty would shift Crowns two of flowers well smelling. Chaucer. 2. To change the place of; to move or remove from one place to… | 1. To divide; to distribute. (old) Some this, some that, as that him liketh shift. Chaucer. 2. To make a change or changes; to change position; to move; to veer; to substitute one thing for another;
sheriffalty: The office or jurisdiction of sheriff. See Shrievalty.
sheephook: A hook fastened to pole, by which shepherds lay hold on the legs or necks of their sheep; a shepherd's crook. Dryden.
shipworm: Any long, slender, worm-shaped bivalve mollusk of Teredo and allied genera. The shipworms burrow in wood, and are destructive to wooden ships, piles of wharves, etc. See Teredo.
shadd: Rounded stones containing tin ore, lying at the surface of the ground, and indicating a vein. Raymond.
shrinker: One who shrinks; one who withdraws from danger.
show: 1. To exhibit or present to view; to place in sight; to display; -- the thing exhibited being the object, and often with an indirect object denoting the person or thing seeing or beholding; | 1. To exhibit or manifest one's self or itself; to appear; to look; to be in appearance; to seem. Just such she shows before a rising storm. Dryden. All round a hedge upshoots, and shows At distance…
shimmer: To shine with a tremulous or intermittent light; to shine faintly; to gleam; to glisten; to glimmer. The shimmering glimpses of a stream. Tennyson. | A faint, tremulous light; a gleaming; a glimmer. TWo silver lamps, fed with perfumed oil, diffused . . . a trembling twilight-seeming shimmer through the quiet apartment. Sir W. Scott.
shrug: To draw up or contract (the shoulders), especially by way of expressing dislike, dread, doubt, or the like. He shrugs his shoulders when you talk of securities. Addison. | To raise or draw up the shoulders, as in expressing dislike, dread, doubt, or the like. They grin, they shrug. They bow, they snarl, they snatch, they hug. Swift.
shawfowl: The representation or image of a fowl made by fowlers to shoot at. Johnson.
shive: 1. A slice; as, a shive of bread. [Obs. or Prov. Eng.] Shak. 2. A thin piece or fragment; specifically, one of the scales or pieces of the woody part of flax removed by the operation of breaking. 3. A thin, flat cork used for stopping a wide-mouthed bottle; also, a thin wooden bung for casks.
sheetcable: The cable belonging to the sheet anchor.
sherry: A Spanish light-colored dry wine, made in Andalusia. As prepared for commerce it is colored a straw color or a deep amber by mixing with it cheap wine boiled down. Sherry cobbler, a beverage prepared with sherry wine, water, lemon or orange, sugar, ice, etc., and usually imbided through a straw or a glass tube.
shot: Woven in such a way as to produce an effect of variegation, of changeable tints, or of being figured; as, shot silks. See Shoot, v. t., 8. | A share or proportion; a reckoning; a scot. Here no shots are where all shares be. Chapman. A man is never . . . welcome to a place till some certain shot be paid and the hostess say "Welcome." Shak.
shoddy: 1. A fibrous material obtained by "deviling," or tearing into fibers, refuse woolen goods, old stockings, rags, druggets, etc. See Mungo. 2. A fabric of inferior quality made of, or containing a… | Made wholly or in part of shoddy; containing shoddy; as, shoddy cloth; shoddy blankets; hence, colloquially, not genuine; sham; pretentious; as, shoddy aristocracy.
shieldless: Destitute of a shield, or of protection. -- Shield"less*ly, adv. -- Shield"less*ness, n.
shadbird: (a) The American, or Wilson's, snipe. See under Snipe. So called because it appears at the same time as the shad. (b) The common European sandpiper. [Prov. Eng.]
shim: 1. A kind of shallow plow used in tillage to break the ground, and clear it of weeds. 2. (Mach.) A thin piece of metal placed between two parts to make a fit.
sherif: A member of an Arab princely family descended from Mohammed through his son-in-law Ali and daughter Fatima. The Grand Shereef is the governor of Mecca.
shakings: Deck sweepings, refuse of cordage, canvas, etc. Ham. Nav. Encyc.
shuffle: 1. To shove one way and the other; to push from one to another; as, to shuffle money from hand to hand. 2. To mix by pushing or shoving; to confuse; to throw into disorder; | 1. To change the relative position of cards in a pack; as, to shuffle and cut. 2. To change one's position; to shift ground; to evade questions; to resort to equivocation; to prevaricate. I muself, .
shough: A shockdog. | See Shoo. Beau & Fl.
shillyshally: In an irresolute, undecided, or hesitating manner. I am somewhat dainty in making a resolution, because when I make it, I keep it; I don't stand shill-I-shall-I then; if I say 't, I'll do 't. | To hesitate; to act in an irresolute manner; hence, to occupy one's self with trifles.
showery: 1. Raining in showers; abounding with frequent showers of rain. 2. Of or pertaining to a shower or showers. "Colors of the showery arch." Milton.
shortstop: The player stationed in the field bewtween the second and third bases.
shrive: 1. To hear or receive the confession of; to administer confession and absolution to; -- said of a priest as the agent. That they should shrive their parishioners. Piers Plowman. | To receive confessions, as a priest; to administer confession and absolution. Spenser.
shog: A shock; a jog; a violent concussion or impulse. [R. or Scot.] | To shake; to shock. [R. or Scot.]
sheriffry: The office or jurisdiction of sheriff. See Shrievalty.
shaman: A priest of Shamanism; a wizard among the Shamanists.
shout: To utter a sudden and loud outcry, as in joy, triumph, or exultation, or to attract attention, to animate soldiers, etc. Shouting of the men and women eke. Chaucer. | 1. To utter with a shout; to cry; -- sometimes with out; as, to shout, or to shout out, a man's name. 2. To treat with shouts or clamor. Bp. Hall.
shirk: 1. To procure by petty fraud and trickery; to obtain by mean solicitation. You that never heard the call of any vocation, . . . that shirk living from others, but time from Yourselves. Bp. Rainbow. | 1. To live by shifts and fraud; to shark. 2. To evade an obligation; to avoid the performance of duty, as by running away. One of the cities shirked from the league. Byron.
shillishalli: In an irresolute, undecided, or hesitating manner. I am somewhat dainty in making a resolution, because when I make it, I keep it; I don't stand shill-I-shall-I then; if I say 't, I'll do 't. Congreve.
sheepy: Resembling sheep; sheepish. Testament of Love.
shopboard: A bench or board on which work is performed; a workbench. South.
shaw: 1. A thicket; a small wood or grove. [Obs. or Prov.Eng. & Scot.] Burns. Gaillard he was as goldfinch in the shaw. Chaucer. The green shaws, the merry green woods. Howitt. 2. pl. The leaves and tops of vegetables, as of potatoes, turnips, etc. [Scot.] Jamieson.
shining: 1. Emitting light, esp. in a continuous manner; radiant; as, shining lamps; also, bright by the reflection of light; as, shining armor. "Fish . . . with their fins and shining scales." Milton. 2. | Emission or reflection of light.
short: 1. Not long; having brief length or linear extension; as, a short distance; a short piece of timber; a short flight. The bed is shorter than that a man can stretch himself on it. Isa. xxviii. 20. 2. | 1. A summary account. The short and the long is, our play is preferred. Shak. 2. pl. The part of milled grain sifted out which is next finer than the bran. The first remove above bran is shorts.
shoaling: Becoming shallow gradually. "A shoaling estuary." Lyell.
shoat: A young hog. Same as Shote.
shingle: Round, water-worn, and loose gravel and pebbles, or a collection of roundish stones, such as are common on the seashore and elsewhere. | 1. A piece of wood sawed or rived thin and small, with one end thinner than the other, -- used in covering buildings, especially roofs, the thick ends of one row overlapping the thin ends of the row…
shopshift: The trick of a shopkeeper; deception. (old) B. Jonson.
she: 1. This or that female; the woman understood or referred to; the animal of the female sex, or object personified as feminine, which was spoken of. She loved her children best in every wise. Chaucer. Then Sarah denied, . . . for she was afraid. Gen. xviii. 15. 2. A woman; a female; -- used substantively. Lady, you are the cruelest she alive. Shak.
shortspoken: Speaking in a quick or short manner; hence, gruff; curt. [Colloq.]
shamoying: A process used in preparing certain kinds of leather, which consists in frizzing the skin, and working oil into it to supply the place of the astringent (tannin, alum, or the like) ordinarily used in tanning.
shoreless: Having no shore or coast; of indefinite or unlimited extent; as, a shoreless ocean. Young.
shovelboard: 1. A board on which a game is played, by pushing or driving pieces of metal or money to reach certain marks; also, the game itself. Called also shuffleboard, shoveboard, shovegroat, shovelpenny. 2. A game played on board ship in which the aim is to shove or drive with a cue wooden disks into divisions chalked on the deck; -- called also shuffleboard.
shed: A slight or temporary structure built to shade or shelter something; a structure usually open in front; an outbuilding; a hut; as, a wagon shed; a wood shed. The first Aletes born in lowly shed. | 1. To separate; to divide. [Obs. or Prov.Eng.] Robert of Brunne. 2. To part with; to throw off or give forth from one's self; to emit; to diffuse; to cause to emanate or flow; to pour forth or out;
shove: 1. To drive along by the direct and continuous application of strength; to push; especially, to push (a body) so as to make it move along the surface of another body; | 1. To push or drive forward; to move onward by pushing or jostling. 2. To move off or along by an act pushing, as with an oar a pole used by one in a boat; sometimes with off.
shabby: 1. Torn or worn to rage; poor; mean; ragged. Wearing shabby coats and dirty shirts. Macaulay. 2. Clothed with ragged, much worn, or soiled garments. "The dean was so shabby." Swift. 3. Mean; paltry; despicable; as, shabby treatment. "Very shabby fellows." Clarendon.

shrewmouse: A shrew; especially, the erd shrew.

sheepback: A rounded knoll of rock resembling the back of a sheep. -- produced by glacial action. Called also roche moutonnée; -- usually in the plural.
shash: 1. The scarf of a turban. (old) Fuller. 2. A sash. (old)

shipmate: One who serves on board of the same ship with another; a fellow sailor.

sharpshooting: A shooting with great precision and effect; hence, a keen contest of wit or argument.
shorling: 1. The skin of a sheen after the fleece is shorn off, as distinct from the morling, or skin taken from the dead sheep; also, a sheep of the first year's shearing. [Prov. Eng.] 2. A person who is shorn; a shaveling; hence, in contempt, a priest. (old) Halliwell.

shittah: A tree that furnished the precious wood of which the ark, tables, altars, boards, etc., of the Jewish tabernacle were made; -- now believed to have been the wood of the Acacia Seyal, which is hard, fine grained, and yellowish brown in color.

shareholder: One who holds or owns a share or shares in a joint fund or property.
shoshones: A linguistic family or stock of North American Indians, comprising many tribes, which extends from Montana and Idaho into Mexico. In a restricted sense the name is applied especially to the Snakes, the most northern of the tribes.
shinshu: The leading and most progressive Buddhist sect of Japan, resting its faith rather upon Amida than Gautama Buddha. Rites and ceremonies are held useless without uprightness.
sharpness: The quality or condition of being sharp; keenness; acuteness.
shepen: A stable; a shippen. (old) The shepne brenning with the blacke smoke. Chaucer.

shooter: 1. One who shoots, as an archer or a gunner. 2. That which shoots. Specifically: (a) A firearm; as, a five-shooter. [Colloq. U.S.] (b) A shooting star.
shrubby: 1. Full of shrubs. 2. Of the nature of a shrub; resembling a shrub. "Shrubby browse." J. Philips.
shalloon: A thin, loosely woven, twilled worsted stuff. In blue shalloon shall Hannibal be clad. Swift.
shabrack: The saddlecloth or housing of a cavalry horse.

shortwited: Having little wit; not wise; having scanty intellect or judgment.

shastasam: A game like California Jack, except that the pack drawn from is turned face down.
shindy: 1. An uproar or disturbance; a spree; a row; a riot. [Slang] Thackeray. 2. Hockey; shinney. Bartlett. 3. A fancy or liking. [Local, U. S.] Bartlett.
sheepish: 1. Of or pertaining to sheep. (old) 2. Like a sheep; bashful; over-modest; meanly or foolishly diffident; timorous to excess. Wanting change of company, he will, when he comes abroad, be a sheepish or conceited creature. Locke. -- Sheep"ish*ly, adv. -- Sheep"ish*ness, n.
shuntwinding: A winding so arranged as to divide the armature current and lead a portion of it around the field-magnet coils; -- opposed to series winding. --Shunt"-wound` (#), a.
shindle: A shingle; also, a slate for roofing. (old) Holland. | To cover or roof with shindles. (old)

sheathless: Without a sheath or case for covering; unsheathed.
